**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Hash mutations before embedding the checkout URL**

When this qualification runs for the same exact HEAD on Ubuntu and Windows—or merely from two different checkout directories—`mutated` contains the absolute `contractsUrl` inserted at lines 155–159, so this SHA changes even though the compiled owner and logical mutation are identical. That makes the per-case mutation hashes host-dependent and unsuitable for comparing independent cross-platform receipts; compute them from canonical mutated owner bytes before the environment-specific import rewrite, or normalize that import first.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include runtime dependencies in the relocated checkout**

When this regression runs after a normal install/build, copying only `packages/contracts/dist` leaves the relocated package without its `ajv` runtime dependency. The `tsc -b` output is not bundled: `packages/contracts/dist/index.js` loads modules that import `ajv/dist/2020.js`, and Node resolves that bare import from the temporary checkout rather than the original repository's `node_modules`. Consequently `qualifyPolicyMutations(copy)` fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` before any hashes are compared, causing the required quality suite to fail; recreate or link the copied checkout's runtime dependencies as part of this fixture.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
